text:
The line graph illustrates the number of people who commuted to work by car, bus and bicycle in a European city from 2000 to 2020.

Overall, car use declined over the period while bus travel rose steadily, so that by 2020 more people travelled by bus than by car. Cycling remained by far the least popular way of getting to work.

In 2000, 420 thousand people drove to work, which was twice as many as those who took the bus (210 thousand). The number of car commuters increased slightly to a peak of 450 thousand in 2005, but after that it fell continuously, reaching 300 thousand in 2020.

By contrast, the figure for buses grew throughout the period. It went up from 210 thousand to 260 thousand in 2010 and then to 330 thousand in 2020, overtaking cars in the last five years. Bicycle use was almost unchanged, staying at around 40 thousand during all the twenty years, with a small rise to 42 thousand in 2005.
